key_insight: On synthetic limit order books, GPT-style models learn predictions consistent with amortized Bayesian inference over market regimes, with generalization driven more by regime diversity than scale.
engineering_relevance: For market-simulation engineering rather than materials discovery, frozen model representations enable accurate, lower-cost simulator calibration and useful transfer to real order flow.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on simulated order flow with known latent parameters and exact data entropy.
Compare predictions against Bayes-optimal and oracle references, including drifting latent regimes.
Probe frozen activations for regime information and test transfer to real NASDAQ data.
evidence_signal: Predictive loss matches the exact Bayes optimum within a millinat per token; frozen read-outs outperform windowed maximum likelihood for calibration, and pretraining beats training from scratch at every tested budget on held-out tickers.
watch_item: Zero-shot performance depends on simulator-prior coverage of real order flow, so synthetic accuracy alone does not establish robustness to unseen market conditions.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
